description: Composite group of seven plots. Five (labelled S1, S2, S3, S4, S5 in the top-left corner) are MatCalc equilibrium phase-fraction vs temperature diagrams for the five steels; the remaining two are RLC-temperature curves labelled S1 and S2. In the phase-fraction diagrams the x-axis is Temperature (°C), spanning 200-1400 (S4 begins at 400, ticks every 200), and the y-axis is Phase fraction on a logarithmic scale with ticks 1, 0.1, 0.01, 0.001, 0.0001. Legend entries are bcc (green) and fcc (red), both with upward arrows; three further curves are labelled κ-carbide (open triangles, ~0.2), hcp (open squares, ~0.004) and (Fe,M)xCy (open circles, ~0.0006). In the bcc/fcc transition window (~700-1000 °C) the green bcc curve falls steeply while the red fcc curve rises. A blue TiC curve appears only in S4. Grey boxes print ferrite-free T_A and carbide-dissolution Tcd: S1 991/1103 °C, S2 929/1107 °C, S3 1177/1103 °C, S4 1016/1134 °C, S5 986/775 °C, with dashed arrows marking the abscissae. The RLC panels plot RLC (%) (0-1.2 for S1, 0-1.0 for S2) versus temperature, with a dashed linear fit crossing a vertical dashed line at Ms = 277 °C (S1) and Ms = 274 °C (S2). Together the panels show that simulated dissolution sequences rationalise the austenitising and Ms temperatures.

observations.observation: Five MatCalc phase-fraction-temperature diagrams are labelled S1, S2, S3, S4 and S5; each uses a logarithmic Phase fraction axis (ticks 1, 0.1, 0.01, 0.001, 0.0001) against Temperature (°C) covering 200-1400 (S4 starts at 400).
In every diagram the green bcc curve falls steeply and the red fcc curve rises steeply within the same ~700-1000 °C window, with green 'bcc' and red 'fcc' arrows pointing to the respective curves.
Each diagram contains curves labelled κ-carbide (open triangles, highest minor fraction near 0.2), hcp (open squares, ~0.004) and (Fe,M)xCy (open circles, ~0.0006).
Grey boxes in the individual diagrams print ferrite-free T_A = 991 °C and Tcd = 1103 °C for S1.
Grey boxes print T_A = 929 °C and Tcd = 1107 °C for S2, and Tcd = 1103 °C with T_A = 1177 °C for S3.
Grey boxes print T_A = 1016 °C and Tcd = 1134 °C for S4, and Tcd = 775 °C with T_A = 986 °C for S5, Tcd being far lower in S5 than in S1-S4.
A blue TiC curve labelled 'TiC' is visible only in the S4 diagram, where it stays at a low fraction and drops near the high-temperature end.

The caption states that the maps show bcc (green), fcc (red) and the κ-carbides, MC, hcp, with TiC appearing only in S4 (blue), and that grey boxes mark the ferrite-free T_A and the carbide-dissolution temperature Tcd.
Two RLC-temperature curves, labelled S1 and S2, are plotted with RLC (%) on the y-axis; each carries a vertical dashed line at a printed Ms value, Ms = 277 °C (S1) and Ms = 274 °C (S2).
The citing text states the simulations indicated ferrite-free T_A values of 991 °C (S1), 929 °C (S2), 1177 °C (S3), 1016 °C (S4) and 986 °C (S5).
The citing text states MatCalc predicted complete dissolution of MC-type (Fe,M)xCy carbides around 1103-1107 °C for S1-S2 and near 1134 °C for S4, and placed Tcd near ~775 °C for S5.
The citing text notes the simulated requirement of ~1177 °C for S3 to approach a ferrite-free state, attributed to the ferrite-stabilizing effect of very high Al.
